newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian Union Bank merges with smaller bank.
newsitem.headline: Estonian Union Bank merges with smaller bank.

text.p: Key Estonian bank Union Bank said it has signed a merger deal with smaller North Estonian Bank to create the country's second largest bank.

Union Bank, quoted both in Tallinn and Helsinki, said in a statement that was released late on Sunday that the merged bank would have total assets of five billion kroons and would have some 24 percent of total Estonian banking assets.

"We are not pursuing size only, the merger fits perfectly with our long-term strategic goal of increasing UBE (Union Bank of Estonia) market share in the most profitable customer segments," Union Bank president Ain Hanschmidt said.
Union Bank said the fit between the two banks was good as Union Bank was dominant outside the capital of Tallinn whereas North Estonian Bank focussed mainly on Tallinn and the northeast of Estonia.
Before the merger, Union Bank was the third largest bank in Estonia and North Estonian Bank was the fifth largest.
The merger is the culmination of a process that began with Union Bank buying a sixth of the North Estonian Bank shares and then putting in a team to help stabilise the bank.
Union Bank said North Estonian Bank's non-performing loans have been written off and would be confirmed by auditors within one month.

It said that the write-offs were fully covered by the owners of North Estonian Bank with the share capital of the bank and by various other assets. It said this meant that the merged entity would begin operations with a clean balance sheet.
Union Bank said the merger would cut administrative costs, eliminate branches and organisational doubling up.
The merger has to be approved by Union Bank's shareholders at a meeting due to take place in February.
